text.name: Defender behaviour monitoring
text.titlePass: Microsoft Defender watches what programs do
text.titleFail: Microsoft Defender does not watch what programs do
text.why: Behaviour monitoring catches malware by what it does, which is the only way to stop malware nobody has seen before.
fix: Tell IT: Microsoft Defender's behaviour monitoring is switched off.
The policy is "Turn on behavior monitoring" under Real-time Protection.

text.name: Defender scan of downloads
text.titlePass: Microsoft Defender scans downloads and attachments
text.titleFail: Microsoft Defender does not scan downloads and attachments
text.why: Most malware arrives as a download or an attachment. Scanning it on arrival stops it before it is ever opened.
fix: Tell IT: Microsoft Defender's scanning of downloaded files and attachments is switched off.
The policy is "Scan all downloaded files and attachments" under Real-time Protection.

text.name: Defender script scanning
text.titleFail: Microsoft Defender does not scan scripts
text.why: Much current malware is a script, not a program file. Without script scanning it runs unseen.
fix: Tell IT: Microsoft Defender's script scanning is switched off.
The policy is "Turn on script scanning" under Real-time Protection.

text.name: Blocking of unwanted apps
text.titleFail: Microsoft Defender does not block unwanted apps
text.why: Unwanted apps are the adware and bundled extras that come with free downloads. They slow the PC and often open the door to worse.
fix: Open Windows Security > App & browser control > Reputation-based protection settings.
Turn on Potentially unwanted app blocking, with Block apps ticked.

text.name: Defender network protection
text.titlePass: Microsoft Defender blocks connections to known bad sites
text.titleFail: Microsoft Defender does not block connections to bad sites
text.why: Network protection stops any program, not just the browser, from reaching sites known for malware and phishing.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Prevent users and apps from accessing dangerous websites", set to Block.

text.name: Attack surface reduction
text.titlePass: Defender's standard attack surface reduction rules block
text.titleFail: Defender's standard attack surface reduction rules are off
text.why: These three rules block techniques that attackers use and ordinary programs do not. Microsoft recommends them for every PC.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules"; each rule shown in the details is set to Block.

rules.name: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers
Block persistence through WMI event subscription

text.name: Defender block at first sight
text.titlePass: Defender holds unknown files until the cloud answers
text.titleFail: Defender lets unknown files run before the cloud answers
text.why: Brand-new malware is in no update yet. Holding it for a few seconds lets Microsoft's cloud judge it before it runs.
fix: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings.
Turn on Cloud-delivered protection: this feature follows it.
If it is on and this still fails, a policy switched the feature off: tell IT.

text.name: Defender sample submission
text.titlePass: Suspicious files are sent to Microsoft for analysis
text.titleFail: Suspicious files are not sent for analysis
text.why: When the cloud needs a closer look, a sample lets Microsoft confirm and block new malware. Held back, the verdict comes late or never.
fix: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings.
Turn on Automatic sample submission.
If the switch is greyed out, tell IT: it is set by policy.

text.name: Defender cloud blocking level
text.titlePass: Defender's cloud blocking level is high
text.titleFail: Defender's cloud blocking level is below high
text.why: At the high level the cloud also blocks unknown files that look suspicious, not only known malware. Rarely, a new genuine program is held back.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > MpEngine.
Set "Select cloud protection level" to Enabled, with High blocking level.

text.name: Defender scan of USB drives
text.why: A USB drive plugged in during a full scan is skipped. Its files are still checked when they are opened.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan.
Enable "Scan removable drives".

text.name: Attack surface reduction for Office
text.titlePass: Office and mail apps cannot launch or plant programs
text.titleFail: Office and mail apps can launch or plant programs
text.why: Most attacks by email start with a document or attachment that starts a program. These rules block that; try in-house Office add-ins first.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules"; each rule shown in the details is set to Block.

rules.name: Block all Office applications from creating child processes
Block Office applications from creating executable content
Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes
Block Office communication application from creating child processes
Block Win32 API calls from Office macros
Block executable content from email client and webmail
Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes

text.name: Attack surface reduction for scripts
text.titlePass: Risky scripts and USB programs are blocked
text.titleFail: Risky scripts and USB programs are not blocked
text.why: These rules stop disguised scripts, scripts that start downloads, unsigned programs on USB drives and files that behave like ransomware.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules"; each rule shown in the details is set to Block.

rules.name: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts
Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content
Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB
